messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1: routing loop during canary rollout detected for policy 'canary-rollout' at 2026-02-16T14:21:08Z. Auto-page on-call. Symptoms: repeated fallback->canary flips across regions, elevated 5xx, client-visible errors. thread_ts=1769312468

pagerduty-bot: Page sent to @alice, @sam (primary oncall), escalation scheduled in 10m if no ack.

alice: I'm on it. Alerts show a spike in 5xx starting ~14:15. Canary variant m-open-v2-qlf is getting 5% traffic and health is flapping. Router logs show repeated "fallback=sticky" then immediate return to canary. looks like flip-flop.

ben: I pulled the router logs. Example pattern repeated: 
`[14:16:02] route decision: canary -> 503 -> fallback sticky -> region=eu-west-1`
`[14:16:03] route decision: retry -> canary -> 200`
`[14:16:03] sticky cookie set -> next request -> canary`
So sticky fallback + very short cooldown is causing bounce.

irene: dumping policy config for the canary-rollout: 
```
routing_policies:
  - name: canary-rollout
    match: "/v1/generate"
    rollout:
      percent: 5
      variants:
        - model: m-open-v2-qlf
          region: us-west-2
        - model: m-open-v2
          region: eu-west-1
    fallback:
      strategy: sticky
      timeout_ms: 200
```

sam: timeout_ms 200 is extremely low — sticky fallback with 200ms cooldown basically re-evaluates immediately. If canary health toggles for a short window, requests will keep switching. We should either increase cooldown or use a different strategy (failover/circuit-break).

deploy-bot: Detected canary rollout ID rr-2026-02-16-0045, pausing rollout per operator request. (action: pause_rollout rr-2026-02-16-0045)

alice: I'm pausing the policy from the console now. Also going to clear sticky session keys for affected prefix. Running: 
```
# list keys for this policy
redis-cli KEYS "route:sticky:canary-rollout:*"
# delete only affected keys
redis-cli KEYS "route:sticky:canary-rollout:*" | xargs -r -L1 redis-cli DEL
```

nora: please don't flush entire sticky cache. only the canary keys as alice is doing. full flush will impact other rollouts.

ben: while alice clears keys, I'm preparing a quick policy patch to stop the sticky behavior and set a longer cooldown. Proposed change: 
```diff
-fallback:
-  strategy: sticky
-  timeout_ms: 200
+fallback:
+  strategy: failover
+  cooldown_ms: 600000  # 10 minutes
```
This forces stable variant until cooldown expires instead of immediate sticky toggles.

irene: customer impact summary (initial): ~3 enterprise customers on dedicated capacity reported latency spikes and some 503s. Approx 120k requests failed (503/502) between 14:15-14:23 UTC. No data leakage. CS notified: @matt_cs.

matt_cs: acknowledged, notifying affected customers with a short heads-up and follow-up once RCA is out.

sam: taking ownership for the next 30m watch. @alice handing off. I'll keep eyes on metrics and logs.

alice: applied the failover + cooldown patch and cleared sticky keys. deploy-bot, can you confirm config applied?

deploy-bot: Policy update applied (id: cfg-2026-02-16-550). Purge job enqueued for route:sticky:canary-rollout:* (job id purge-789).

ben: metrics: error rate falling from 11% at peak -> 1.2% over 3 minutes after policy change and cache purge. Request latency also trending down. No new flip entries in the router logs.

sam: confirming from the dashboard: canary now stays routed to stable variant; no loop observed for 5 minutes. Keeping watch for 30m.

irene: quick postmortem notes: probable root cause = interaction of aggressive sticky fallback (200ms timeout) + canary health flapping under load. The routing logic immediately returned traffic to canary once it served a 200, but sticky keys persisted causing immediate re-routes and oscillation. Two fixes: (1) change default fallback strategy for rollouts to failover with cooldown, (2) bump default cooldown_ms to at least 5m for small percent canaries, (3) add circuit-breaker that halts sending new canary traffic after N transient errors in short window.

alice: created incident doc https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-045 with timeline and mitigation steps. I'll own the RCA ticket for configs.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by @sam. Escalation timer cancelled.

sam: confirmed stable at 14:34:25 UTC. I'll watch until 15:05 and then hand back to normal ops. Follow-ups: update rollout defaults, add tests for sticky fallback timing, and ensure console warns on sub-1s cooldown.

nora: also recommend a canary health-debounce setting (e.g., require 3 consecutive successes before reintroducing) — I'll file a ticket.

alice: thanks everyone. Good catch on the sticky keys. Closing thread when metrics are green for the watch window. :thumbsup:
